title: Parse Status Message
prompt: A TypeScript client receives a discriminated result from an API. Write a function that returns the success message when status is "success" and the error message when status is "error".

explanation.beginner:
Example: parseStatusMessage({"status":"success","message":"Saved"}) produces "Saved". Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Compare “reads error messages”: input [{"status":"error","error":"Try again"}] produces "Try again". Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Map each explicitly supported state to its exact output text or value. Separate state selection from formatting.

Tempting mistake: Capitalization, whitespace, and boolean-versus-string output are part of the contract; truthiness alone may combine distinct states.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “reads error messages”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
